richtext.heading: Why a CMS Is No Longer Enough
richtext.lead: A CMS manages content. A DXP orchestrates experiences. Here's what that difference means in practice.
richtext.name: Richtext
richtext.sidebarText: Not sure if DXP AI is right for your organization? Our solutions team can help you evaluate your current stack, identify gaps, and map out a migration path — no pressure, no sales tactics.
richtext.text:
1. Scope: Pages vs. Journeys

A CMS manages individual pages. DXP AI orchestrates end-to-end customer journeys across web, mobile, portal, email, and voice — with consistent personalization at every touchpoint.

2. Intelligence: Static vs. Adaptive

A CMS serves the same content to everyone. DXP AI uses ZensAI behavioral intelligence to adapt every experience in real time — based on who the user is, what they've done, and what they're likely to do next.

3. Integration: Siloed vs. Connected

A CMS requires expensive custom integrations to connect to your CRM, ERP, or analytics stack. DXP AI ships with 50+ enterprise connectors and an open API framework that makes your entire tech stack work as one.

4. Analytics: Vanity Metrics vs. Actionable Insights

A CMS gives you page views and bounce rates. DXP AI gives you funnel analysis, predictive lead scoring, content attribution, and AI-generated recommendations — so you can act, not just report.

5. AI Capability: Bolt-On vs. Built-In

Adding AI to a legacy CMS means stitching together third-party tools with limited context and no unified data model. ZensAI is the engine at the core of DXP AI — not an afterthought.

section_light.heading: How DXP AI Compares
section_light.name: Section Light
section_light.text: See how DXP AI stacks up against the leading enterprise platforms.

item_0.heading: DXP AI
item_0.name: Features Item
item_0.text: AI-native from the ground up. ZensAI intelligence built into every module — content, personalization, search, analytics, and operations. Composable architecture with 50+ connectors. 30-day free trial. Fastest time-to-value in the market.

item_1.heading: Adobe Experience Manager
item_1.name: Features Item
item_1.text: Powerful and mature platform with deep Adobe ecosystem integration. Complex implementation, high licensing cost, and significant time-to-value. AI capabilities bolted on via Sensei — not native. Best suited for large enterprises with deep AEM expertise.

item_2.heading: Sitecore
item_2.name: Features Item
item_2.text: Strong personalization and experimentation capabilities. Fragmented product portfolio post-acquisition. High TCO and complex composable architecture requires significant dev investment. AI via third-party integrations.

item_3.heading: Liferay
item_3.name: Features Item
item_3.text: Excellent for employee and partner portals with strong Java ecosystem. Limited marketing capabilities and AI features. Better suited for internal experience platforms than customer-facing DXP deployments.
